page: OVHcloud a10-90 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance engineered for high-throughput parallel compute and deep learning workloads. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, the platform provides 60 dedicated x86_64 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9554 processor clocked at 3.3 GHz. The configuration allocates one thread per core without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring predictable CPU performance. Hardware vector extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and bfloat16 support, complementing the compute subsystem alongside 85 GB of system memory.

Hardware acceleration is delivered by two bundled NVIDIA Ampere A10 GPUs offering a combined 48 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. Storage is provisioned via an integrated 400 GB local SSD, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier throughput across multi-threaded operations, including a multi-core stress-ng score of 187018.94 and a PassMark CPU score of 92461.97. LLM inference benchmarks confirm top-tier performance across varied model sizes, achieving 2784.61 prompt tokens per second and 90.5 generation tokens per second on 7B models, as well as 10.67 generation tokens per second on 70B models.

Resource allocation presents a specific operational tradeoff: the memory-to-core ratio is compact at approximately 1.42 GB per vCPU, while the 400 GB local SSD provides constrained working space for large datasets. As a result, the instance favors compute-dense workloads rather than vast in-memory processing. Cost efficiency is optimized for parallelized pipelines requiring dedicated dual-GPU throughput alongside dense AMD EPYC execution without enterprise-grade host memory overhead.
OVHcloud a10-90 is suited for mid-sized large language model serving, distributed inference, AI batch processing, 3D graphics rendering, video transcoding, and parallel continuous integration builds.

Hardware acceleration features two NVIDIA Ampere A10 GPUs delivering 48 GB of total VRAM, supplemented by 400 GB of local SSD storage and a 16 Gbps baseline network interface. The server allocates a lean 1.42 GB of RAM per vCPU, prioritizing raw parallel compute over expansive memory footprints. This architecture makes the instance cost-efficient for AI model serving, machine learning inference, parallel software compilation, and graphics rendering workloads.
